policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV makes the law the subject of a singular verb: 'the law ... can never ... make perfect', matching singular δύναται. The mapped textual_variant note 'Many ancient authorities read they can' explicitly relegates the plural δύνανται to the margin.
κεκαθαρισμένους and κεκαθαρμένους are alternative perfect passive participle forms of the same verb with identical sense; ASV 'having been once cleansed' renders either, and no note touches the form.
ASV reads plural 'Sacrifices and offerings', matching Θυσίας καὶ προσφορὰς; the singular Θυσίαν καὶ προσφορὰν would yield 'Sacrifice and offering'.

English 'according to the law' requires the article regardless; anarthrous νόμον in a prepositional phrase is equally definite in Greek, so ASV wording does not distinguish νόμον from τόν νόμον, and no note is mapped here.
ASV has 'Lo, I am come to do thy will' with no vocative; the RP addition ὁ θεός would appear as 'O God', which the ASV does not print here or in a note.

The added article οἱ before ἐσμὲν leaves the clause 'we have been sanctified' unchanged in English; the only note on the verse is classed alternative_rendering ('Or, In') and concerns the preposition, not this unit.
οὗτος and αὐτὸς are both rendered 'he' in ASV's 'but he, when he had offered'; the verse's only note is classed alternative_rendering about the placement of 'for ever' and cannot decide a reading.
ASV reads 'for after he hath said', with no element answering the προ- prefix; προειρηκέναι would give 'after he had said before'.
ASV reads singular 'upon their mind', matching τὴν διάνοιαν; the RP plural τῶν διανοιῶν would give 'their minds'.
ASV prints the clause 'then saith he,' at the close of v.16, immediately before 'And their sins' — that is ὕστερον λέγει, which only r01 contains; the base reading offers no words for it.
μνησθήσομαι (future) and μνησθῶ (aorist subjunctive after οὐ μή) are both rendered 'will I remember no more'; ASV wording does not distinguish them and no note is mapped here.
ASV runs 'I will recompense. And again,' with nothing for λέγει κύριος; the RP addition would print 'saith the Lord' after the quotation.
The variants differ only in the order of verb and subject; both yield ASV's 'The Lord shall judge his people', which follows normal English order either way.
ASV reads 'had compassion on them that were in bonds' — persons, i.e. δεσμίοις (prisoners) — not the RP 'my bonds' (δεσμοῖς μου), which would supply a first-person possessive the ASV nowhere prints.

ASV text reads 'ye have for yourselves a better possession', the dative ἑαυτοῖς; the mapped textual_variant note gives the accusative construction 'ye have your own selves for a better possession' (ἑαυτοὺς) as the marginal alternative, confirming the text follows r01.
ASV reads 'a better possession and an abiding one' with no locative phrase; the RP addition ἐν οὐρανοῖς would print 'in heaven', which appears neither in text nor note.
The variants differ only in the order of adjective and noun; ASV's 'great recompense of reward' renders either order identically.
ASV text reads 'But my righteous one shall live by faith', rendering μου; the mapped textual_variant note 'Some ancient authorities read the righteous one' assigns the omission to the margin.
